clue.text: Game Boy not opening for Oliver Stone

indicators.note: 'not' tells us a letter is to be left out of the word beside it
'opening for' keeps only the first letter of 'Oliver'

blocks.note: RU is short for rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A film director gets an advert for a handheld games console without its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Stone the film director is split: 'Oliver' supplies the O dropped from BOY, and 'Stone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious gem, and gems are called stones.

clue.text: Maybe Martin Luther King in favour of cracking Times cryptic

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscured, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
to crack something is to break into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: R for Rex, Latin for king
to be for something is to be in favour of it

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the civil rights leader would have enjoyed a newspaper's cryptic crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martin Luther King' reads as one name, but King is wordplay (R) and only Martin Luther is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation, so he is an example of a reformer; 'Maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Comedian in New York absorbed by Twin Peaks

indicators.note: whatever is absorbed by something ends up inside it

blocks.note: two words for a peak: a ben is a Scottish mountain

explanation.surface: A comedian in New York gets hooked on the TV series Twin Peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Twin Peaks looks like the David Lynch TV show, but it means two separate peaks, BEN and HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian famous for his slapstick sketch show.

clue.text: Bass provides introduction for Everybody Dance

indicators.note: an introduction is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A bass line kicks off a track telling everyone to get dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering held for dancing.

clue.text: Nick Cave finally accepting this number is tending to grab attention

indicators.note: 'finally' points at the last letter of the word beside it
accepting something means taking it in, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: to nick is British slang for to arrest
this clue is number 4, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The singer Nick Cave's song holds the listener's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Cave the singer is split: Nick means arrest, and Cave gives its final letter. 'This number' is the clue's own number, 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrestive describes something striking that stops you in your tracks and seizes notice.

clue.text: City has energy-saving lights

indicators.note: saving something keeps it safely held within

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A city has installed low-energy street lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy-saving' reads as one green adjective, but it means the lights hold the energy symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Husky remains guarding one big bundle of nerves

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it protectively

blocks.note: bran is what remains of husked grain

explanation.surface: A husky's remains are protected by a very nervous person.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky seems to be the dog, but it is the adjective meaning of husks.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ where the body's nerve tissue is most concentrated.

clue.text: Swimmer closing in on rest

indicators.note: closing in on something wraps around it

blocks.note: a bather is someone who swims

explanation.surface: A swimmer is approaching a break in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause to rest and recover.

clue.text: Flood in a toilet rising over belly of cowboy

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top
the belly is the middle, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the middle of rancher, a cattle-ranching cowboy

explanation.surface: A cowboy's belly sits above an overflowing toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the earlier pieces sit above the later one.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming rush of something, so a flood in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Relative majority of Greece in flip-flops

indicators.note: only most of the following words is used, so the letters lie inside them
to flip-flop is to turn about, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the end of Greece and in run together

explanation.surface: Most relatives in Greece wear flip-flops, or so the claim goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative majority' poses as an electoral term, but Relative alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Picked up juvenile bird

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so we want a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: a minor is a juvenile; in a British accent it rhymes with China

explanation.surface: Someone collected a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The mynah is a starling-family songbird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Uncommitted lover on the loose around Cyprus

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so a piece sits inside the rest

blocks.note: a fan is a lover of something

explanation.surface: An unattached lover is running wild in Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free means not in love or tied down to anyone.

clue.text: Duck in English Channel going west

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Dave is a British TV channel

explanation.surface: A duck swims across the English Channel heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: English Channel is not the sea: English is E and Channel is the British TV station Dave.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to avoid it, a synonym of evade.

clue.text: Is that Illingworth with Boycott's glasses?

explanation.surface: Is that cricketer Ray Illingworth wearing Geoffrey Boycott's spectacles?
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Illingworth and Geoffrey Boycott were Yorkshire and England cricketers; here Boycott is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray-Bans are a well-known brand of sunglasses.

clue.text: Titus Oates oddly missing dreadful place

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, so only the even ones stay
something dreadful is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of Oates

explanation.surface: Titus Oates, the notorious Popish Plot conspirator, has vanished from some dreadful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Oates loses its odd letters; Titus stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to put it in position, to place it.

clue.text: Jot letter to Grecian

blocks.note: first meaning: a very small amount
second meaning: a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Grecian is the setter's pseudonym, so the clue also reads as a note to the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the smallest Greek letter, which is why it also means a tiny scrap.

clue.text: Puritan upset about new date for cricket game

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rest goes inside

explanation.surface: A puritan is annoyed about a fresh date for a cricket fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip and run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the bat touches the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip and run is an informal knockabout version of cricket played in back gardens.

clue.text: Slaver not using right tool

indicators.note: not using a letter means leaving it out

explanation.surface: A slave trader refuses to use the correct implement.
explanation.walkthrough: Slaver looks like a slave trader, but it is the verb meaning to drool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dibble is a pointed hand implement for making holes to plant seedlings.

clue.text: ... is Dancing Queen here?

blocks.note: surface: carrying on from 3, asking whether the queen of the dance floor is present
setter's reading: callers say 'Dancing Queen' for the number 17, from the ABBA lyric 'only seventeen', and this clue is 17

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 3 across, 'Everybody Dance'; bingo callers have nicknames for each number, and ABBA's song gives seventeen its call.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers are called out in a venue built for that gambling game, where 'Dancing Queen' means seventeen.

clue.text: See 21
Meta deployed under-18 security experts

indicators.note: troops deployed are rearranged into position, so the letters move

blocks.note: 18 across is CAT, and a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: The company Meta has hired some teenage computer-security staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-18' reads as a minor, but it means placed below a type of 18 in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger team is a group hired to test an organisation's defences by trying to break in.

clue.text: Train dog with ducks for weeks

indicators.note: X for Y means put X in place of Y

blocks.note: the chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog
a duck is a score of nought, O, so two of them
W is short for week, so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone trains their dog with ducks for weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like a verb, but it is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Choo-choo is a childish word for a railway engine, from its sound.

clue.text: Leader of the gang to get cheap stuff for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts trade places

blocks.note: to cop is to get, and tat is cheap stuff; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: The gang boss sends someone out for some knock-off goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of cop tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Cat is the cartoon alley cat who leads his gang in the Hanna-Barbera series.

clue.text: Prostitute with uninitiated person performing task in bed

indicators.note: uninitiated means lacking its start, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A prostitute and an inexperienced client get down to business in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not where the surface puts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoeing is weeding soil with a garden tool, a chore done in a flowerbed.

clue.text: Mountain bird briefly returns

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
returns means comes back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A bird comes back briefly to a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg is a mountain in South African usage, and short for an iceberg, a floating ice mountain.

clue.text: Unlimited funds for present

indicators.note: without limits means without its ends, so only the inside stays

explanation.surface: Endless money for a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance, to offer it.

clue.text: Dismiss from post

blocks.note: first meaning: order off, as a referee does a player

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like firing someone from a job, but the post is mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee dismisses a player by sending him off, and you dispatch a letter by sending it off.

clue.text: James Bond perhaps talked abruptly about love

indicators.note: abruptly means cut off suddenly, so the end letter goes
about means around, so the rest wraps the other piece

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: James Bond curtly discusses romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is slang for a spy, and Bond is a fictional secret agent; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Something frivolous from female Pulitzer Prize winner

blocks.note: Philip Roth won the Pulitzer for American Pastoral

explanation.surface: A lightweight work by a woman who won the Pulitzer.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is light, insubstantial entertainment or talk with no depth.

clue.text: Turner ultimately following John Constable?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is kept

blocks.note: john is slang for a lavatory, and the offices is an old euphemism for one

explanation.surface: The painter Turner came after John Constable among English landscape artists.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner and Constable are both great English painters, but Constable is the police rank here.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of police officer; the question mark flags the shift from painter.

clue.text: King pair essentially the end of Dominic Cork's fun?

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so only the central letters stay
the end means the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles

explanation.surface: Two kings are at the heart of the cricketer Dominic Cork's amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominic Cork was an England cricketer, but Cork is the Irish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Craic is Irish for good times and lively chat, so it is what people enjoy in Cork.

clue.text: Chat show featuring comeback of silent star

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Harpo Marx never spoke on screen

explanation.surface: A talk show features the return of a silent-film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oprah Winfrey Show was the hugely popular American television talk programme.

clue.text: Typically badly peeled navel orange

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outer letters go
badly means done wrong, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: As usual, the navel orange has been peeled poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only navel is peeled; orange stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually, as a general rule.

clue.text: Comedian missing two days in combat

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so letters are taken out

blocks.note: D is short for day, twice

explanation.surface: A comedian has missed two days of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: See 2
Mischievous child endlessly making racket

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A naughty child is endlessly making noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket suggests din, but it is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme, a con or fraud.
